contradictions.fact: Total round-trip distance for the Standard Route

claims.says: Given the ~45 km round trip and glacier travel, this is realistically a multi-day trip...
A 4-day glacier backpack, roughly 34 miles and 8,500 ft cumulative gain round trip...

contradictions.why: Three fields give three different round-trip distances for the same route: dist_km implies ~16.3 mi, the approach text says '~45 km round trip' (~28 mi), and the itinerary's day-by-day miles sum to ~34 mi (~55 km) — no two of the three agree.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoints' own cumulative one-way distance to the summit (14 mi) doubles to ~28 mi/45 km, matching the approach text almost exactly; the itinerary's higher total plausibly includes the Old Guard Peak side-summit tagged the same day; dist_km (~16.3 mi) is roughly half the implied round trip and appears to be the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Length of the rappel below the summit

claims.says: ...a short Class 4 step here requires downclimbing or a 100-150 ft rappel.
Most parties rappel this step — a single 150 ft rope covers both the lead and the rappel, and anything over 100 ft of rope is adequate for the ~100-150 ft rappel.
1 rappel (~50-75 ft) off a tree anchor; a 150 ft rope covers both the roped pitch and the rappel - doubled through the tree a 100 ft rope reaches only about 50 ft.
...rappelling the one short (~50-60 ft) class 4 section...
Class 4 (~50-60 ft)
A 150 ft (45 m) rope covers both: 30 m is long enough to LEAD the short step but not to rappel it, since doubled through the tree anchor it reaches only about 49 ft.

contradictions.why: Four fields describe a ~50-75 ft rappel done on a 150 ft rope doubled through a tree anchor, while the waypoint and descent_text both call the same rappel 100-150 ft — but a 150 ft rope doubled can only reach ~75 ft, so a 100-150 ft rappel is arithmetically impossible with the technique and rope length the rest of the route describes.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The doubled-rope math in rope_note/rappels (150 ft rope ÷ 2 ≈ 75 ft max reach) supports the 50-75 ft figures; the waypoint's/descent_text's 100-150 ft claim is inconsistent with that same 150 ft rope.

contradictions.why: The header pitches field says 1, but the ROUTE BREAKDOWN table (pitch_detail) lists two rows.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Only one of the two rows (the roped 'Summit step') is a true belayed pitch; the other is unroped Class 2-3 travel, which may explain the count but isn't distinguished by the field itself.

'Summit Middle Peak' / 'Summit North Peak' (no true summit, no rope work mentioned)

contradictions.internal_resolution: At least eight other fields (waypoints, descent_text, rappels, pitch_detail, gear, rock_grade, approach, baseFinding) describe reaching the true 5,814 ft summit; the itinerary's day-2 plan is the outlier and matches the route baseFinding explicitly warns against.
